test_title: SSC CPO 2022 Tier-II Official Paper (Held On: 02 May, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in blank number 4.
solution:
The correct answer is** 'So'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The context of the blank 4 requires a conjunction that provides a reason or an effect. The sentence preceding this is stating the high value of a Ph.D.
 
• 'So' is a conjunction used to introduce clauses of result or decision, and in this context, it gives the reason why the university maintains high-quality standards.
 
• The use of 'so' here shows that because the Ph.D has a high value, the university, as a result, maintains a high quality.
 
• Therefore, using 'so' makes the sentence read as "So, the university maintains the quality at a very high level," which correctly interprets the intended meaning of the sentence.

**Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• 'Because': Generally used to introduce a reason or justification, it doesn't fit here as we're referring to a result, not a cause.
 
• 'Although': Used to introduce a subordinate clause expressing a concept that potentially contradicts the information provided in the main clause - not suitable here.
 
• 'Since': Can be used to provide a cause, but 'so' fits better as we're discussing a result or decision.
